transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?
I guess… lately I just feel like I’m always moving from one thing to the next. Like I can’t really just sit and idle. And with the new setup at work, it’s been harder to kind of cover that up.
Would you say this feeling of always needing to be moving or busy has been part of who you are since you were a kid, or is this something that's really only started recently?

No, it’s not really new. I guess looking back it was there when I was a kid too. Teachers would put things on my report cards like I was bright but careless… talked when I shouldn’t, needed reminders to stay on my work. Stuff like that.
Besides feeling like you always need to be moving, do you also notice things like blurting out answers, interrupting others, or having a hard time waiting your turn in conversations or lines?

Yeah… sometimes. At work, if I hear someone trying to figure out a customer issue, I’ll kind of jump in with the answer before they’re done talking. I don’t mean it in a rude way, but… yeah, I do that.
Do you notice these same kinds of difficulties—like trouble focusing, jumping ahead, or feeling restless—outside of work too, like at home or in your personal relationships?

Yeah… some. At home it shows up more with quiet things, I guess. Like if I’m trying to read, I don’t get very far before I’m shifting around. Or if my wife and I watch a movie, I’ll end up making comments or getting up for something. I don’t really just sit through it.

Would you say these patterns—jumping in, restlessness, trouble focusing—have actually caused problems for you, like at work or in your relationship, or is it more just something you notice about yourself?

Yeah… I guess it’s caused some problems. Mostly at work. It’s come up in my reviews a bit—unfinished tickets, mistakes that slow other people down. I’m trying, and I usually do okay with customers, but… yeah, they’ve pointed it out.

Have you ever had distinct periods—lasting days or weeks—where this restlessness or trouble focusing got much worse and was accompanied by things like a very elevated or irritable mood, decreased need for sleep, or excessive worry, and then periods where it got better?
I don’t think so. I mean… it’s kind of always been there, not like some separate stretch of days where I’m suddenly way different. I haven’t really noticed that pattern.
Thinking back, do you remember these same kinds of restlessness, distractibility, or impulsivity being noticeable before you were about 12 years old?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, looking back, it wasn’t just this job or anything. In grade school I remember teachers saying I was bright, but careless… talked out of turn, had to be reminded to stay on my work. That kind of thing.
